ai_summary: Scotland continues to demonstrate an exemplary low-emission power profile today, maintaining a Scottish carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh compared to 61 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Across Great Britain as a whole, wind output has reached 12.0 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 1.0 GW, representing 9.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Despite this clean baseline, structural transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and major southern demand centres continue to force renewable energy off the system. Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 204 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £6,641. Because this zero-carbon generation could not be transported across constrained grid boundaries, thermal generation was dispatched to compensate, resulting in an estimated 38,741 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and releasing an additional 71 tonnes of CO2. Extrapolating today's constraint expenditures indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £2 million. Distributed across national electricity demand, this financial constraint burden translates to an estimated increase of less than £0.01/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, underscoring the urgency of strategic grid reinforcement to eliminate network curtailment and reduce end-consumer costs.
